# 1. Small Multiple

Cargamos el archivo que sacamos de aquí: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/mohankrishnathalla/mobile-reviews-sentiment-and-specification

```{r}
df <- read.csv("Mobile_Reviews_Sentiment.csv", stringsAsFactors = TRUE, 
                                 fileEncoding = "latin1")
```

```{r}
# Convertir model en factor (para controlar el orden si quieres)
df$model <- as.factor(df$model)

# Agrupar por modelo y rating y contar ocurrencias
rating_counts <- df %>%
  group_by(model, rating) %>%
  summarise(count = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Gráfico small multiple de líneas
ggplot(rating_counts, aes(x = factor(rating), y = count, group = model)) +
  geom_line(color = "#0073C2FF", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(color = "#0073C2FF", size = 1.5) +  # puntos opcionales para mayor claridad
  facet_wrap(~ model, ncol = 4, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribución de Ratings por Modelo",
    x = "Rating",
    y = "Conteo"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 1) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 8),
    axis.title = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 8),
    axis.text = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 8)
  )
# Histograma de precios por modelo
ggplot(df, aes(x = price_usd)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 15,            # número de rangos (puedes ajustar)
    fill = "#0073C2FF",   # color tipo Tableau
    color = "white"       # bordes blancos para estética
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ model, ncol = 4, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribución de Precios por Modelo (USD)",
    x = "Precio (USD)",
    y = "Conteo"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 1) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 8),
    axis.title = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 8),
    axis.text = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 8)
  )

```

# 2. Flow Map

Cargamos el archivo que sacamos de aquí: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jacekpardyak/openflights?select=airports.json

```{r}
# --- Cargar datos ---
routes <- fromJSON("routes.json")

# Filtrar rutas que salgan de aeropuertos españoles
routes_es <- routes %>%
  filter(grepl("Madrid", src))

# --- Cargar mapa base de Europa ---
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
europe <- subset(world, subregion %in% c("Southern Europe", "Western Europe", "Northern Europe", "Eastern Europe"))

# --- Crear puntos intermedios para arcos suaves ---
routes_es <- routes_es %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    mid_lat = (src_lat + dst_lat)/2 + 5,  # eleva el arco
    mid_lon = (src_lon + dst_lon)/2
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# --- Preparar datos para geom_bezier ---
routes_bezier <- routes_es %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  do(data.frame(
    src = .$src,
    dst = .$dst,
    lon = c(.$src_lon, .$mid_lon, .$dst_lon),
    lat = c(.$src_lat, .$mid_lat, .$dst_lat)
  )) %>%
  ungroup()

# --- Graficar mapa con arcos suaves ---
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = europe, fill = "grey20", color = "white", size = 0.2) +
  geom_bezier(
    data = routes_bezier,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, group = interaction(src, dst)),
    linewidth = 0.3,
    color = "deepskyblue",
    alpha = 0.4
  ) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-25, 35), ylim = c(25, 70)) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "black", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "black", color = NA),
    plot.title = element_text(color = "white", hjust = 0.5, size = 8, face = "bold")
  ) +
  ggtitle("Vuelos desde Madrid")



# Filtrar rutas que salgan de aeropuertos españoles
routes_fr <- routes %>%
  filter(grepl("Paris", src))

# --- Cargar mapa base de Europa ---
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
europe <- subset(world, subregion %in% c("Southern Europe", "Western Europe", "Northern Europe", "Eastern Europe"))

# --- Crear puntos intermedios para arcos suaves ---

# --- Preparar datos para geom_bezier ---
routes_bezier <- routes_fr %>%
``` 

# 3. UpSet: Visualizing Intersecting Sets

Cargamos el archivo que sacamos de aquí: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/mohankrishnathalla/mobile-reviews-sentiment-and-specification

```{r}
df <- read.csv("Mobile_Reviews_Sentiment.csv", stringsAsFactors = TRUE, 
                                 fileEncoding = "latin1")
```

```{r}
# Lista de marcas que queremos graficar
brands <- c("Google", "Apple", "Xiaomi", "Realme")

plot_upset_by_brand <- function(brand_name, df) {
  
  # Filtrar datos de la marca
  df_brand <- df %>% filter(brand == brand_name)
  
  if(nrow(df_brand) == 0){
    message("No hay datos para la marca ", brand_name)
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Número total de reviews
  n_reviews <- nrow(df_brand)
  
  # Crear variables lógicas (TRUE/FALSE) según rating >= 4
  df_upset <- data.frame(
    good_battery = df_brand$battery_life_rating >= 4,
    good_camera = df_brand$camera_rating >= 4,
    good_performance = df_brand$performance_rating >= 4,
    good_design = df_brand$design_rating >= 4,
    good_display = df_brand$display_rating >= 4
  )
  
  # Convertir TRUE/FALSE a 1/0
  df_upset_num <- as.data.frame(lapply(df_upset, function(x) as.numeric(x)))
  
  # Graficar UpSet
  upset(
    df_upset_num,
    sets = c("good_battery", "good_camera", "good_performance", "good_design", "good_display"),
    keep.order = TRUE,   # respeta el orden de sets
    order.by = "freq",
    main.bar.color = "#0073C2FF",
    sets.bar.color = "#4DBBD5FF",
    text.scale = c(1.5, 1.5, 1.2, 1.2, 1.2, 1.2),
    mainbar.y.label = paste("Intersecciones para", brand_name),
    sets.x.label = "Número de reviews buneas"
  )
}

# Generar un gráfico por marca
for(b in brands){
  print(plot_upset_by_brand(b, df))
  # Filtrar datos de la marca
  df_brand <- df %>% filter(brand == b)
  
  if(nrow(df_brand) == 0){
    message("No hay datos para la marca ", b)
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Número total de reviews
  n_reviews <- nrow(df_brand)
  print(paste("Número total de reviews para", b, ":", n_reviews))
}

```
